Endlich wieder ein vernünftiges Battlefield! 

Nach mittlerweile weit über 600 Spielstunden kann ich mit absoluter Überzeugung sagen: Das Warten hat sich gelohnt. Wer die Serie über die letzten Jahre verfolgt hat, weiß, dass wir eine lange Durststrecke hinter uns haben – aber dieser Teil macht verdammt vieles richtig und bringt das klassische, großzügige All-Out-Warfare-Gefühl zurück, das wir so vermisst haben.

Klar, um ehrlich zu sein: Der ganz spezielle, unverkennbare Vibe aus den glorreichen Zeiten von Battlefield 3 und Battlefield 4 fehlt an der einen oder anderen Stelle noch ein kleines bisschen. Aber – und das ist das Wichtigste – das Spiel kommt diesem genialen Core-Gameplay extrem nahe! Das Gunplay fühlt sich knackig an, die Zerstörung hat wieder echtes Gewicht und das Zusammenspiel im Squad macht einfach süchtig.

Die Maps bieten die gewohnte epische Kulisse und das Balancing hat sich nach den letzten Updates hervorragend eingependelt. Es fühlt sich einfach verdammt gut an, abends die Kiste anzuschmeißen und zu wissen, dass man eine authentische, packende Battlefield-Erfahrung geliefert bekommt.

Für Veteranen der Reihe und für Shooter-Fans, die nach einem echten Sandbox-Kriegsgebiet suchen, eine absolute Kaufempfehlung. Wir sehen uns auf dem Schlachtfeld!

Spielstunden: Genug, um meiner Frau zu erklären, dass das „keine Sucht, sondern Fortbildung“ ist.

Schauen Sie. Ich bin ja nun in einem Alter, wo man sich beim Bücken nach einer runtergefallenen Socke vorher kurz überlegt, ob man da unten nicht direkt ein neues Leben aufbauen sollte. Und dann kommt Battlefield 6.

Ich habe es gestartet. Und was soll ich sagen? Es ist gut. Es ist wirklich gut. Aber es ist auch ein emotionaler Whirlpool aus „Mein Gott, ist das herrlich!“ und „Wer hat den Designern eigentlich ins Müsli geniest?“.

Hier ist mein völlig unaufgeregter Zwischenbericht aus der Schützengraben-Hölle:
Die Filetstücke (Was wirklich Laune macht)

    Die Optik: Mein PC hat beim Laden der ersten Map Geräusche gemacht wie eine Kaffeemaschine, die versucht, ein Hufeisen zu zersägen. Aber das Ergebnis? Eine Augenweide. Wenn da ein Hochhaus einstürzt, sieht das so realistisch aus, dass ich instinktiv meine Haftpflichtversicherung anrufen möchte.

    Das Mittendrin-Gefühl: Das Spiel schafft es wie kein zweites, dieses Gefühl von absolutem, majestätischem Chaos zu erzeugen. Du liegst im Schlamm, über dir explodiert ein Jet, links schreit einer nach seiner Mama, und rechts versucht ein Teamkollege, einen Panzer mit einer Signalpistole zu erlegen. Das hat beinahe etwas Meditatives. Wenn man den Puls von 180 mal kurz ausblendet.

Die Dellen im Blech (Wo es hakt)

    Die Menüführung: Wer auch immer das User Interface verbrochen hat, gehört nachts um drei barfuß in eine Kiste voller Lego-Steine geschickt. Ich wollte lediglich meine Grafikkarte entlasten und habe aus Versehen die Vorwahl von Bottrop eingegeben und ein Abonnement für eine schwedische Landwirtschaftszeitung abgeschlossen. Es ist kompliziert.

    Das Balancing: Die Entwickler dachten sich wohl: „Komm, wir geben den Spielern Waffen, die streuen wie eine defekte Gießkanne, aber die Scharfschützen treffen dich aus drei Kilometern Entfernung durch die geschlossene Klotür eines Dixi-Klos.“ Da stehst du dann. Getroffen von einem Projektil, das wahrscheinlich noch im letzten Jahrhundert abgeschossen wurde.

Fazit

Ist es perfekt? Um Himmels willen, nein. Es hat Ecken und Kanten wie ein schlecht geraspelter Block Blockmalz. Aber es hat Seele. Es ist diese Art von Spiel, bei dem man sich drei Stunden lang furchtbar aufregt, um danach direkt die nächste Runde zu starten, weil man der Meinung ist, dass der Typ im gegnerischen Team einen ganz persönlich beleidigt hat.

Kaufen Sie es sich. Aber stellen Sie sich ein kaltes Getränk bereit. Für die Nerven.

Natural to enable console players to be competitive against mouse+keyboard (lets not forget, its a shooter and M+K is superiour in this field) the game industry invented aim"assist".
Its basicly an aimbot, plain and simple.
The aimassist is so much hardcore overtuned, that, no matter what weapon you use on console, you have zero recoil, very very forgiving aiming and the skill to delete other players across the map with an SMG. Combine that with very low TTK times in this game and you have a balance mess and CoD gameplay.
The PC players NEED TO plug in a controller to make some use of the console aimassist to some degree to be competitive (and lets not forget the sweats).

Battlefield 6 had the potential to become one of the best shooters on the market. The game delivers massive battles, chaos, and gameplay that sits nicely between arcade action and realism. Unfortunately, like every modern multiplayer game, there is always a giant “but”.

Before launch, the developers promised grounded military cosmetics. Instead, we got skins that sometimes feel like rejected Call of Duty operator bundles. The camouflage system is also disappointing. I have no problem with artificial intelligence being used in development, but after seeing the same mesh pattern painted in fifty slightly different shades, even my soldier probably wants a wardrobe change.

The gunplay is a thing that makes my feelings about this game mixed. During the open beta, the shooting felt smooth and responsive. After launch, however, firefights became a little strange. Sometimes you get shot behind walls, sometimes you die before your brain even registers that someone looked in your direction.

Still, despite its flaws, the game is genuinely fun. Battlefield 6 captures the large-scale chaos the series is known for while staying accessible to casual players. If you want a shooter that feels arcade-like without turning into complete nonsense, this game does a solid job.

The launch was successful, and the 2026 roadmap looks promising. With naval warfare arriving in Season 4, there is still plenty of potential here.

Battlefield 6 has serious issues with account progression and paid content stability. I purchased the Phantom Edition and used a mix of BF Coins and earned in-game currency to unlock content, which was previously available on my account.

After a recent update, multiple unlocked items relocked themselves and became inaccessible. I contacted EA Support and was told they could not restore the content due to a 30-day game sync limitation, leaving no solution for recovering purchased or unlocked items.

For a game with paid editions and microtransactions, losing access to previously unlocked content with no recovery option is a major issue. Until these account and entitlement systems are made reliable, I can’t recommend spending money on in-game purchases.

Core gameplay may be fine, but the progression and entitlement system is not dependable.

I have always been a big fan of the Battlefield series, been playing since BF1942 when you needed to load 1/2 dozen CDs just to install. Personally I think the series peaked with BFV

That being said, this feels less like old BF and more like they tried to copy the pace of CoD. A lot of weapon specs make no sense, many SMGs will outgun a rifle at range, and LMGs all do very little damage whether because of dmg or fire rate (support being my favorite class) which gets you outgunned by everything.

A lot of monetization has been introduced so be prepared to open the wallet if you want to keep up with equipment, otherwise you're waiting till the end of the season to get the newest weapons/gear, and there is a lot of weapons.

Also, the netcode seems to have some issues such as dying to gunfire after you've already made it behind cover. I personally live on a tiny island right now and having no servers here I am reliant on connecting up to the mainland over 1,000 miles away, because of this I pretty much lose any corner surprise gun fights making the game very not fun.

In short, if you like CoD, you will probably like this BF as it is faster paced than pretty much all previous versions, but make sure you are fine with either paying a lot of money every season for new content or being satisfied with the base stuff, and make sure you don't live on a tiny island with bad internet and 1k+ miles of latency.

Most scopes are awful (there's like 30), and every scope you actually want to use (a handful) are locked behind hours of playing with terrible ones. It's not fun to be forced to use a bad scope or a zoom level you don't want.

Also:
- the UI is terrible (clunky and not remotely intuitive)
- there's like 1,000 settings but no search feature, you have to manually look through them all 
- it's very grind heavy to unlock weapons and attachments (feels like it was made for unemployed people)
- it costs $70 and they still want you to buy seasonal battle passes

- sniping:
If you're used to sniper rifles in any other FPS game you're going to be irritated. You have to unlock and always use a certain attachment (the ADS bolt) in order for the snipers to function how you expect them to. If you don't use the ADS bolt attachment then this is how shooting any of the sniper rifles works (there are no semi-auto sniper rifles, all of them are bolt action):

BF6 sniping without the ADS BOLT attachment
1) right click to look through the scope
2) left click to shoot 1st shot
3) left click again to stop looking through the scope and cycle the bolt to chamber another round
4) right click to look through the scope again
5) left click to shoot 2nd shot

Equipping the ADS BOLT removes steps 3 and 4 making sniper rifles work like they do in literally every other FPS game.

There's no setting you can change to make it automatically unscope and cycle the bolt, you're forced to manually click the fire button a second time every time. It's a very hard habit to get into if you're used to sniping in other games. You're constantly going to think you can click again to fire a 2nd shot but instead of firing, it's going to unscope and chamber a new round. But hey, at least they made the ADS bolt take a long time to unlock and made it one of the most expensive attachments (equipping it means you won't be able to use all the other attachments you want to equip).

Battlefield is visually stunning and has great potential, but the gameplay experience is currently broken due to extreme latency dependency.
The Problem: Netcode & High Ping
The game relies entirely on your connection. Even a 1ms difference in ping creates a massive disadvantage that is clearly noticeable during gunfights. My experience has been terrible because:
• TTK (Time to Kill) is inconsistent: I often find myself shooting first and landing an entire magazine into an enemy's chest, only for them to turn around and kill me instantly.
• Desync: On my screen, I am hitting them, but due to the ping, the server doesn't register the damage.
Server Status
Since the Middle East servers were closed, I am forced to play with a ping of 80ms. While this might seem "average" in some games, in Battlefield, it makes the game practically unplayable and unfair.
Final Verdict
I cannot recommend Battlefield in its current state. If you don't live right next to a server, you will struggle. It’s incredibly frustrating to lose matches simply because of network infrastructure rather than skill.
Avoid this game until they address the server issues for our region.

**BF6 = AMAZING GAME RUINED BY FORCED CROSSPLAY**

Battlefield veteran since Battlefield 1942, and honestly… this game COULD have been the perfect Battlefield.

BUT they completely ruined it for PC players with one thing:
FORCED CROSSPLAY.

PC players CANNOT disable crossplay. No option. Nothing. So you are permanently forced to play against console players abusing ridiculously overpowered aim assist that feels straight-up like legal aimbot.

If PC players had the option to turn crossplay OFF, this game would honestly be incredible.

Instead, every fight feels fake:

* console players tracking perfectly through smoke and recoil (which is heavily reduced on console)
* instant lock-on at close range
* zero human error thanks to aim assist doing half the work

And on top of that:

* terrible netcode
* random hit registration
* constant desync
* dying meters behind cover

How do you make gunplay-focused FPS games for 20+ years and STILL have netcode this bad?

Maps are mid overall, except Siege of Cairo which is actually fun.

What frustrates me the most is that the core game is GOOD. The atmosphere, destruction, sounds, movement… it’s all there. But forced crossplay completely destroys the experience for PC players.

This could have been the perfect Battlefield. Instead, it’s another frustrating mess.

I normally do not write reviews at all, but had to for what i've seen,

Battlefield 6 had a rough start. At launch, it felt incomplete—maps were too small, the focus seemed to be on microtransactions, more specifically a free-to-play battle royale mode rather than delivering the core Battlefield experience. For a lot of modern releases, that kind of launch can feel like the game is destined to be abandoned.

However, 8 months in, the developers have shown a real commitment to listening and improving. The game has grown in ways that actually matter: bigger maps, meaningful updates, and a clear focus on fixing the gameplay rather than chasing trends. It feels like the devs are truly redeeming the game and building toward what it should have been at launch.

What I really appreciate is that, even with the microtransactions, they’ve kept things grounded. Everything added fits the military theme—no cartoonish cosmetics, no anime guns, no magic bullets, no celebrity skins—just the authentic Battlefield vibe.

If this trajectory continues, I genuinely believe that one year post-launch, BF6 will feel like a completely different, fully realized game. It’s exciting to see a franchise I love being treated with this level of care and attention, and I’m optimistic about the future.

8/10 now, with the potential to climb higher as the updates continue. This is a game worth revisiting and keeping an eye on.

Easily one of the best shooters available currently, and a pretty great battlefield. I have had 250 hours so far and will have a lot more during the lifespan of the game. A lot of the criticism doesn't ring true to me, or is exaggerated in my opinion. There is some fair criticism that I agree with:

-The maps are a bit small, but not as bad as some people make out, this is still far from COD and the new maps are much bigger. It does play faster than the older games though so be aware. 
-The old premium model was better than the new battlepass model, and progression for a casual player is a bit slow. 
-The gun balance is a bit strange with SMGs still being pretty good at range whilst some assault rifles struggle. I always use a mix of guns though so it doesn't bother me much. 
-The biggest actual complaint that affects my actual experience was half-empty lobbies being back-filled by bots instead of players. This was a real problem for a long while (6 months ish) but seems to be fixed now (fingers crossed).

  Mostly though I've had a great time. Not watching or engaging with social media has no doubt helped as there is lots of content out there designed to make people annoyed. I played BF1942, BFBC2, BF3 a lot, BF1 a lot, BF5, some BF2042, and now this. This is a mostly great game, and still provides an experience unique to Battlefield. 

  The visuals are fantastic, the audio is amazing, the gunplay is great, sniping feels excellent, the performance has been excellent for me (maxed settings on a high end rig). If you really enjoy battlefield then I would just buy this and enjoy it, and ignore most of the noise surrounding it. You don't need BF Pro so don't worry about buying the battlepass unless you really want to.

BF1, c’était le genre de jeu où même en perdant tu restais dans la partie parce que l’ambiance était folle.

Dort machen die Kämpfe nach knapp 10 Jahren immernoch spaß und optisch sehen die beiden Teile noch dazu viel besser aus. Außerdem hat man mit den behemoths aus dem ersten Teil ein cooles feature eingebaut, sodass das benachteiligte Team immernoch ein Chance hat das Match zu wenden. In Battlefield 6 spielt sich jeder Modus identisch und es gibt nichts an das man sich noch später erinnert. Gunplay, Sound, Chaos stimmen für das moderne Setting – aber es fehlt die Battlefield‑Identität, die früher ganze Abende legendär gemacht hat. So ist es leider wie jeder andere Shooter. I’ll start with the positive things first. The open beta was really fun, especially when playing in a squad with friends. It made me forget the disaster of BF 2042 for a moment. The intense fights, the heavy explosions, and the close‑quarters combat were stressful, but in a good way.

But now, after two seasons, my friends and I can clearly see where this Battlefield is heading. All matches feel the same. Enemies always use the same CoD‑like weapons (mostly SMGs or assault rifles), and everyone only plays for their KD. Class roles are rarely used the way they should be. The spawn system is terrible — I spawned next to enemies in our own area so many times. It’s more run & gun than strategic gameplay, which worked much better in the older games. The maps are too small and everything looks bland and repetitive. Matchmaking is also useless; you usually win or lose with a 500–800 ticket difference. Some maps are completely unbalanced depending on which side you start on.

People who are unhappy with Black Ops 7 will probably enjoy this game. But I’m done. I’ll return to the old battlefields in Battlefield 1 and 5. Those games are still fun even after almost 10 years, and they still look better. BF1’s behemoths were a great feature that gave the losing team a real chance to turn the match around. In Battlefield 6, every mode feels the same and there’s nothing memorable about it. The gunplay, sound, and chaos are good for a modern setting — but the Battlefield identity is missing. The identity that once made whole evenings unforgettable. Now it feels like every other shooter. You won’t find teamplay, tactical depth, or large‑scale battles here anymore.

Where to begin with this game.
First, a disclaimer. I play mainly Conquest, and sometimes branch out into other gamemodes. But I would wager 95% of my playtime is in Conquest, and as such my opinions are based almost exclusively on that one gamemode (and a little bit of rush)

Being a Battlefield veteran, playing Battlefield 2 on the family PC as a child, but having most of my playtime in Bad Company 1/2, and BF3 and 4, this game is in no way a perfect Battlefield game, but it is absolutely a step in the right direction after the last couple of entries to the series.

Season 3, with the release of Golmud, makes the game feel more like BF3 and BF4 than any other entry since those two. But, because of course there's a but, this one map that has the feeling and gameplay of a proper Battlefield map does not make up for the many shortcomings of the game.

Recoil still feels soulless on all weapons, with only minor differences between every weapons handling.
Basically every map feels pretty much the same, with the typical 3 lane layout, with limited proper flanking routes. The verticality of many of the maps is also quite lacking, and the maps with verticality are often not by design, but just people getting on top of massive rocks or mountains in the middle or edges of the maps, and sitting there for the entire game. Those rocks are also a part of the design problem, with the 3 lane design I mentioned earlier. The rocks or mountains make up the split between the lanes, and feel like exactly that: a design choice to divide the map right down the middle, which feels soulless and artificial.
Besides the 3 lane layouts of many of the maps, there is also just a major lack in variety of the maps. All of the maps can be put into 3 major categories (and one minor category that only Golmud fits into).
The first of these categories i call "Close quarters spamageddon" reminiscent of Operation Metro but without the actually fun map layout, the second is "Somewhat big empty death trap", and the final major category I call "Generic city centre map".
The fourth category, exlusively fitting Golmud for now, is "Somewhat varied and balanced large map", and this category is in my opinion what the map designers should strive for with most of the maps.
Golmud is, at this very moment, the absolutely best map in the game in my opinion. Vehicles are in abundance, and can be easily countered if you have competent teammates (and half a brain yourself). The map has large empty areas, but there are lanes between the points and through the empty areas, with a variety of cover for infantry. The map is in no way perfect, but it is the only actually [i] fun [/i] map in the game at this moment for me. I am however biased towards vehicle gameplay, both ground and air, so take this opinion with a grain of salt if you yourself prefer infantry gameplay.

The gameplay itself, however, is quite fun. The gunplay isn't perfect, but it's much more engaging and fun than BF2042. The movement is fast, but not too fast, and feels smooth. And thank god the operator system is gone.
The performance of the game is alright. My setup runs most maps at almost ultra settings, 1440p, at around 80-120 fps, but some of the larger maps, especially Golmud, can dip to about 60 fps later on in the round.

With all of that said would i recommend the game? At full price: hell no. Stay away from the 70€ price tag. I bought it for 42€ I believe, and at that price I'm closer to recommending the game. In it's current state however, the price point I believe the game is worth is roughly €30, and no higher. The biggest reasoning for this is the lack of interesting maps.

Also two things to be aware of:
The amount of whining in the in-game chat is unbearable. I recommend turning it off completely.
Crossplay can't be turned off on PC. Not that I personally have a problem with playing against people using controllers. I do however have a problem with the fact there simply is no in-game option to turn crossplay off for PC players.

What I appreciate most is how active the developers are. You can clearly see they're listening to the community and constantly patching the things that actually annoy players. The game feels cared for and it's getting better with every update. That's rare these days and it makes me want to keep coming back.

The gameplay itself is exactly what I want from Battlefield: dynamic, fast paced, and chaotic in the best possible way. Big maps, proper vehicle play, intense infantry fights, and those "only in Battlefield" moments that still happen regularly. It feels like the series has finally remembered what made it special.

The endless comparisons to BF4 are honestly getting a bit tiring. 
It's the same thing people did with every new Heroes of Might and Magic after Heroes 3 - treating the old game like an untouchable legend. Yes, BF4 was amazing, but that doesn't mean this game can't be great in its own way. I'm having more fun here than I had in years with the series.

If you enjoy fast, destructive, large-scale multiplayer shooters, Battlefield 6 is in a really good place right now. Definitely worth jumping in.

Battlefield 6 é um completo inferno pra quem acompanha e joga as seasons, toda temporada adicionam duas coisas e quebram cinco. 
Vou resumir, dizem que vão arrumar o netcode mas continua a mesma coisa, dizem que vão reduzir o tempo para matar (ou TTK) mas não fazem nem questão de tocar na velocidade de projétil direito, a bola da vez é a performance e o gunplay.

Não deveria ser difícil fazer um jogo como BF6 rodar em uma maquina 6 cores 12 threads.

Há outros pontos importantes.
-> Quem joga no console sempre tem algum tipo de vantagem no cross-play, seja pelo netcode ou o recoil reduzido (não confunda com assistência de mira). 
-> O gunplay agora tem recoil aleatório, o tiroteio virou um jogo gacha.
-> Boa parte dos mapas são impopulares com a comunidade e só serve pra encher linguiça.
-> A visibilidade continua ruim.

Não é atoa que tão apelando pra mapa dos jogos antigos como Grand Bazaar (BF3) e Golmud Railway (BF4) pra ver se conseguem restaurar a playbase no método da nostalgia, mas não adianta, a DICE precisa parar de tentar fazer a gameplay do jogo ser algo fútil e raso.

Então, por favor, PELO AMOR DE DEUS SÓ TRAGAM DEVOLTA O GUNPLAY DO BF3, BF4 ou BF1, não deveria ser um parto para vocês.

Ruined by Season 3 update. Anything that could possibly even scratch the paintwork of a vehicle has been nerfed whilst the vehicles themselves have then been made even more powerful. Expect to see literally everyone having to play engineer as tanks and IFVs slaughter everyone, sponging infinite rocket hits, literally deleting mines at the press of a button (the same mines that no longer have a prayer of killing said vehicles). DICE seem to only care about vehicle users, and want to remove any impediment to their unstoppable killstreaks. Infantry are merely fodder now.

I absolutely loved this game on release, played battlefield for a decade, love it to bits. But this season 3 update is nothing but coddling to vehicles (which I use, I want vehicles to be powerful when used correctly), as DICE themselves have basically made it impossible to misuse vehicles. Not realising that maybe a tank shouldn't be able to drive into a terrible situation and somehow win every time. That maybe an IFV shouldn't be able to detect mines without even having to bother looking for them (yet somehow people think that is more skillfull than those using mines).

Netcode was fine on release, actually the best on any Battlefield. But then people scapegoated it and DICE for some reason listened to them.

Claymores no longer kill. Javelin still dives into the ground constantly. And despite the "diminishing returns" promised with multiple repairers on one vehicle, the increased vehicle health cancels this out.

DICE for years have been incapable of game balance. Rather than buffing the weaker stuff to match the stronger stuff (the best way to do things), they will do this simultaneously with a nerf on what was considered powerful. So all of a sudden something goes from OP to useless. THAT IS NOT BALANCE.

The Season 3 patch has taken a game I loved to play, that got me hanging out with people I hadn't seen in years. And turned it into an appalling unbalanced vehicular moshpit. Where somehow vehicle users get a free pass in playing poorly whilst infantry have to go above and beyond to even have a cats chance in hell of stopping them. The vehicle imbalance now makes BF4s fall update look tame by comparison.

I can only assume those at DICE are vehicle mains who aren't far off adding invincibility to them.

Battlefield titles are usually best at release, before DICE start fiddling with things with their complete incapability of balancing things even remotely correctly.

Playing with my friends is now the only reason why I may consider booting this up again, and even then its a CHORE to play. And whilst there's a tiny chance this update has been a huge mistake, I know DICE well enough to not hold out for a correction. In a matter of hours, one of my genuinely favourite games of all time has become dross on my hard drive.

And I know there's a lot of the community rejoicing at this update for some reason. And when DICE inevitably ruin your fun, I don't want to hear it, I've protested this stuff for years. You can lie in the bed of your making.

Gameplay is fine. Generally enjoyable. Some frustrating things, some good parts. They did put quite a bit of attention to detail, which was nice. This brings me to why I'm writing this review: unless you play no other games, have a monster of a large PC (SSD space I mean) or are okay with organising your PC according to BF6 updates, don't bother. 

For so much attention to detail, they either: have THE WORST FILE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM IN DIGITAL HISTORY or are the most underhanded, profit-seeking studio that wants you to play no other game besides theirs (which, given that its EA....). Why do I say this? The minimum spec is 55GB required to install. The recommended is 80GB. The actual installed size on my system is 126GB. This is, if you are like me and like to occasionally go back to play the campaign. There is a multiplayer-only install as well. So, size discrepancy aside, this means NOTHING when a new season comes along. New maps, guns, etc. - all the nice goodies. One problem though? It needs an ADDITIONAL, give or take, 150GB ON TOP OF THE EXISTING 126GB!!! That is 276GB space dedicated to BF6 every damn new season. Now keep in mind, while not explicitly stated, you do not want to try run this game on an HDD. That means it has to go on your primary drive (SSD) .

For the average user who has a 512GB drive: 40GB is used by system files/OS, leaving you with about 470ish GB. An additional 50 GB is necessary as a virtual workspace for your PC (unless you want it to crash every 15min). That leaves you with 420GB. That means you effectively have 144GB after BF6 is installed and needs to update for all your videos, music, projects, photos, work programs and files. Perhaps doable, right? Except you are forgetting all those background files that optimising programs don't remove (if you are even running one of those), and that the average game size varies between 30GB -70GB. So good luck uninstalling all those other programs/games every new season if you want to keep playing BF6. (Or you could completely uninstall BF6 then redownload it. That does save a lot of space).

Now, don't get me wrong. The game is, from my perspective at least, genuinely enjoyable. But that hassle every 3 months - hence the rant. Why the actual hell do they need 150GB to update game files... It makes no bloody sense...

Después de 30 horas de juego debo decir que l0a campaña de Battlefield 6 es corta y floja, mientras que el multijugador entrega momentos buenos, pero su diseño de mapas y ritmo no se termina de sentir la magia de Battlefield como en BF3/BF4.
La campaña se siente baja en duración y ambición, es breve y olvidable, sin momentos memorables ni narrativa potente, es una experiencia que se puede terminar rápida y sin engancharte. 

El multijugador sí funciona y puede llegar a ser muy entretenido, ya que, se mantiene  la intensidad y combate ágil, pero falla en recuperar totalmente el espíritu de las entregas clásicas. Menos libertad táctica y menos espacios enormes para vehículos y combates a largo alcance como en BF3/BF4.

Espero que se solucione un poco esto del multijugador con la temporada 3, que tiene mucho provecho para sacarle, fuera de todo esto, es un battlefield y la gente lo jugara solo por ser un battlefield, pero aveces se siente como si el juego le faltara cariño o como si quisiera competir cuando no lo necesita en mi opinión.

Ni hablar del battleroyale Warzone es mejor y no sabría decir porque.... Quizás es costumbre.

Battlefield ruhunu geri getiriyoruz diye çıkıp ortaya yine kimliksiz bir karma bırakmışlar. Eskiden Battlefield dediğin şey; kaosun içinde takım oyunu, atmosfer ve “savaş hissi” demekti. Şimdi ise biri kanat takıp uçuyor, diğeri haritanın öbür ucundan kayıyor, ortalık TikTok montajı gibi olmuş. Serinin ağırlığı ve ciddiyeti resmen buhar olmuş durumda.

En kötü tarafı da oyunun artık “Battlefield anı” yaşatmaması. BF3, BF4 dönemlerinde tank sesi bile adrenalini yükseltirdi. Şimdi çatışmalar plastik gibi hissettiriyor. Haritalar büyük ama ruhsuz, silah hissiyatı tat vermiyor, savaş atmosferi yerine cosplay arenası havası var.

Anti-cheat konusu zaten tam trajikomedi. Daha birkaç maçta garip hareketler yapan adamlara denk geliyorsun. İnsan “acaba gerçekten iyi mi oynuyor yoksa sistem yine uyuyor mu” diye düşünmeden edemiyor. Rekabet hissi yerine güvensizlik oluşuyor.

Grafik ve efekt tarafında güzel duran anlar var ama sadece görüntü oyunu kurtarmıyor. Battlefield serisi bir zamanlar sektör standardıydı, şimdi ise eski oyuncuların hafızasında kalan anıların gölgesinde yaşamaya çalışıyor gibi. Nerde o eski BF’ler dedirtiyor gerçekten.

Como que um jogo tão caro consegue ser tão mal otimizado? Montei um PC forte, investi pesado no hardware justamente pra conseguir jogar tudo no alto sem dor de cabeça, e mesmo assim essa bomba não consegue entregar FPS estável. O pior é que nem dá pra aproveitar gráficos melhores porque o jogo começa a travar de um jeito ridículo.

Pra mim, Battlefield morreu no BF1. Hoje parece que lançam jogo incompleto, mal otimizado e empurram atualização depois, enquanto quem comprou no lançamento vira testador pagando preço cheio.

E o mais revoltante é isso: meu PC passa dos requisitos recomendados com sobra, e ainda assim não consigo ter gráficos bons e FPS estável ao mesmo tempo. Sinceramente, é lamentável. Se quem tem máquina forte já tá sofrendo, imagina quem tem setup mais simples tentando rodar isso.
